title: LP2-00–02: audit the 729 ÷ rune-index proposal
question: Does the posted 729 divided by GP-index rule reproduce its worked first word and specify a complete output on the 729-rune section?
summary: The 729-rune count is correct, but the worked example uses index 28 for prime 107, which has zero-based index 27. F makes division undefined at 34 positions; line clock and wrap choices change hundreds more outputs.

family.title: LP2 cross-section index inversion
family.question: Can the reported 729/index arithmetic be reproduced with one complete set of input and line rules?

scope.representation: Every archived rune of LP2-00–02 in printed line order, GP prime values and zero-based 29-rune indices. The source's eight first-word indices are fixed in the plan, including its 28 for prime 107.
scope.procedure: Verify the 729-rune count, then for every nonzero index j calculate floor(729/j), remainder, base index modulo 29, and the posted fractional threshold with both global and page-reset line counts. Keep both raw and wrapped candidate indices; mark zero-index F undefined. Compare the first eight source indices and labels with the claimed worked example.
scope.parameters: Three pages, 33 source rune rows, exact rational fractional comparisons, line numbering from one, no word rearrangement or removal. Modulo-29 wrapping is an explicitly additional convention for comparison, not a source claim.
scope.exclusions: A fixed rule for F; chosen neighboring letters; letter rearrangement or dummy-word removal; image-level review of every rune; a full plaintext or a statistical language claim; other 729-based constructions.

finding: All three pages contain 729 runes, but the claimed first-word index for prime 107 is 28 rather than its canonical zero-based 27. Literal arithmetic with the archived rune gives Y rather than the report's AE at that position. The 34 F runes have index zero and no quotient. Without wrapping, 335 of 695 non-F outputs fall outside the alphabet under global line counting; global and page-reset wrapped outputs differ at 396 of 695 positions.
limitations: The supplied post names no complete F handling, wrap rule, global-versus-page line clock or deterministic selection from its neighboring letters. Its excerpted image is unavailable; this audit identifies the post by hash and uses the archived transcription. The chosen full-stream conventions are declared extensions and do not recreate all manual postprocessing in the discussion. Human review pending.
next_steps: If pursuing this method, freeze zero handling, line clock, wrap and branch selection before reading output; preserve punctuation and all 729 rune positions, then test complete text and an untouched continuation under matched controls.

reproduction.environment: Python 3.12 standard library; no network or AI service. Run from the repository or extracted bundle root.

review.reviewer: Codex — all-position source and exact-fraction oracle, prime-table check, two line conventions and independent first-word audit; human review pending
